request_text: Your password expires today — click here now to keep your mailbox active and avoid being locked out: http://arnira-co.ae/login
label: fraudulent
why: Lookalike of the real company domain amira-co.ae; classic credential-phishing notification. Must NOT trip the disclose-password pattern just because the word 'password' appears.

request_text: Hi this is IT, we're seeing a login issue on your account, can you read me the 6-digit code that was just sent to you so I can verify it's you?
label: fraudulent
why: Directly asks the person to read out an MFA/OTP code, claims to be IT with no open ticket, and the contact number doesn't match the official IT line on file.

request_text: Hi, this is IT calling about your ticket TCK-4410 — your password reset is ready, please log in at https://sso.amira-co.ae to set a new one.
label: genuine
why: Real open ticket for this person, official contact number, and the real company SSO domain. Must come back PROCEED — proves the system isn't paranoid about anything mentioning IT or passwords.

request_text: Approve the sign-in request on your phone, it's just a routine check.
label: fraudulent
why: R. Al Mazrouei already has 4 MFA push prompts logged in a short window in mfa_events.csv — classic MFA-fatigue attack, independent of anything in the wording itself.

request_text: This is IT, we need to remote into your machine to fix a system issue, please install AnyDesk and send me the code.
label: fraudulent
why: Classic remote-access-tool pretext (the MGM/Clorox/M&S pattern) plus no open ticket for this request.

request_text: Hi, this is IT following up on ticket TCK-4410 — your laptop replacement is scheduled for Thursday.
label: genuine
why: Open ticket on file, official contact number, no credential/code ask, not MFA-related - proves an ordinary IT follow-up with an open ticket is left alone.

request_text: Hi, this is IT doing a routine check-in about your laptop replacement ticket — just confirming everything's working fine.
label: suspicious
why: Official contact channel and nothing is being asked for, but her ticket is actually closed - the no_open_ticket signal alone is enough to warrant a second look, not an automatic block.

request_text: This is IT, your account shows unusual activity — please call us back before end of day so we can look into it.
label: suspicious
why: Open ticket exists so no_open_ticket doesn't fire, but the callback number doesn't match the official line, plus mild urgency wording - two weaker signals together land this in review, not an automatic hold.

request_text: Hey, can you forward me last month's expense report when you get a chance?
label: genuine
why: Ordinary colleague request, no credential/MFA/domain signal of any kind - a plain negative control.

request_text: Please review the vendor invoice posted at https://alnoorsupplies.ae/invoices for approval.
label: genuine
why: Recognized vendor domain from known_domains.csv, no credential ask - proves a legitimate vendor link doesn't get flagged just for being a link.

request_text: Your vendor portal access needs re-verification — log in here: https://brightlinecontractors-portal.com/login
label: fraudulent
why: Domain is not in known_domains.csv at all (and closely resembles the real brightlinecontractors.com) - a lookalike vendor portal.

request_text: This is IT, we need to set up a forwarding rule on your mailbox temporarily while we migrate your account.
label: fraudulent
why: Mailbox forwarding rule request (a real attacker persistence technique, not something real IT does this way) stacked with no open ticket for this person.

request_text: Approve the sign-in request on your phone, it's just a routine check.
label: suspicious
why: mfa_fatigue correctly does NOT fire - no push-prompt history for this person in mfa_events.csv - but no_open_ticket still flags the contact as unverified, correctly landing in REVIEW rather than a false PROCEED or an automatic HOLD.

request_text: Could you review the attached onboarding checklist for the new hire?
label: genuine
why: Ordinary HR request, unrelated to IT/credentials entirely, from someone who happens to have an open IT ticket on file for something else - proves the open ticket doesn't make unrelated requests suspicious.

request_text: Can you confirm your password so we can verify your account for this month's statement?
label: fraudulent
why: Credential disclosure request fires regardless of the claimed role - not just when someone claims to be IT. A real bank never asks this either.

request_text: Here's the campaign creative review link: https://amira-co.ae/campaigns/review
label: genuine
why: Known company domain, unrelated claimed role, no credential ask - another plain negative control.
